main_diagnosis: Two primary problems are likely driving the very poor fit (high negative log-marginal NLE): (1) a critical error in the internal noise scaling inside the time-stepping loop that injects dt-dependent, unrealistically large stochastic currents; and (2) the simulator only uses one of the two extensible channel slots and both flexible params are consumed by the single M-type K channel, leaving the model unable to flexibly tune spike threshold/subthreshold depolarization (a small persistent inward current is commonly needed to match spike count and subthreshold statistics for tonic spiking). Fixing the noise implementation and adding a parsimonious X2 (persistent Na / INaP) channel while reassigning the flexible parameters should substantially reduce the observed mismatch.

issues.description: Incorrect scaling of the stochastic current inside the main time loop: the code divides by sqrt(dt) instead of multiplying, producing noise amplitude that grows as dt->0 and producing unrealistic dt-dependent variability in voltage traces.
issues.location: forward(): inside time-stepping loop — the noise_term assignment (noise_term = nois_fact * torch.randn(...) / (tstep ** 0.5))
issues.suggestion: Replace the division by sqrt(dt) with multiplication by sqrt(dt) (or otherwise treat nois_fact as a per-ms noise intensity and use sigma * sqrt(dt) * N(0,1)). For example: noise_term = nois_fact * torch.randn(batch_size, generator=generator, device=device) * (tstep ** 0.5). Also consider: (a) document whether nois_fact is intended as current-noise amplitude per sqrt(ms) or per ms and name it accordingly; (b) move observation noise into nois_fact_obs (or expose it) and keep a clear distinction between process noise (in-loop) and observation noise (final return). Finally, ensure reproducibility by seeding the generator once per forward pass (current approach is fine) and avoid reseeding inside the loop.

issues.description: Under-utilization of the available channel capacity and lack of a persistent inward current: the code consumes both flexible parameters for X1 (M-type K) and leaves X2 unused (gbar_X2 is present but unused). Without a small non-inactivating inward current (e.g. persistent Na / INaP) the model has limited ability to shift spike threshold or raise subthreshold depolarization to match spike counts and voltage mean/variance.
issues.location: forward(): extra-channel implementation section (X1/X2 handling) — X2 (gbar_X2) is unused and param_j is only applied to X1
issues.suggestion:
Implement a parsimonious X2 as a persistent sodium-like current (non-inactivating or very slowly inactivating) and use the remaining flexible parameter(s) to tune it. Example design: 
 - Use gbar_X2 = params[:,7] as the conductance scale for INaP. 
 - Map one flexible param (e.g. param_j) to a physiologic V_half_X2 (e.g. in range -90..-20 mV) or to a small tau if you want slow activation; use a small slope k_p (5-8 mV). 
 - Compute instantaneous activation p_inf = 1/(1 + Exp((V_half_X2 - V)/k_p)) (optionally update with a slow tau if desired). 
 - Add gbar_X2 * p (or gbar_X2 * p * E_Na) to the conductance and current sums (i.e. include gbar_X2*p in tau_V_inv and gbar_X2*p*E_Na in V_inf_num). 
 - Keep INaP conductance modest so it modulates threshold and subthreshold mean/variance without producing bursting or sustained high-frequency firing. 
Reassign parameters so that X1 and X2 each get clear roles (e.g. param_i -> V_half_X1, param_j -> V_half_X2 or tau_X2). This will increase model expressivity in a targeted, parsimonious way and should help match spike counts and the voltage summary statistics.
